sentences._hearing_file: Kalu Ram vs State Of Rajasthan on 15 January, 2024.json

sentences.text:
The present application under Section 389 Cr.P.C. for suspension of sentence has been filed seeking suspension of the sentence, awarded to the applicant-appellant vide the judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 26.07.2022 passed by the learned Special Judge, Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 & Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005,
No.1, Pali in Sessions Case No.56/2021, whereby while convicting the applicant-appellant for the offences under Sections 366, 342 and 376 (1) IPC, the applicant-appellant was ordered to undergo 05 years, 06 months and 10 years rigorous imprisonment, respectively, alongwith a fine of Rs.10,000/-, Rs.500/- & [2024:RJ-JD:1084] (2 of 4) [SOSA-59/2023] Rs.10,000/- respectively, in default of payment of which, the applicant-appellant was ordered to undergo simple imprisonment for a further period of 03 months, 15 days & 03 months, respectively; all the substantive sentences were ordered to run concurrently.
sentences._hearing_file: Kalu Ram vs State Of Rajasthan on 15 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: 2. Learned counsel for the applicant-appellant submitted that learned Court below passed the impugned judgment on the basis of FSL and DNA reports, but such evidence in this case is not conclusive proof, wherein the victim is a married lady and thus,
sentences._hearing_file: Kalu Ram vs State Of Rajasthan on 15 January, 2024.json

sentences.text:
the sentence awarded to the applicant-appellant vide the impugned judgment, which was passed solely while relying on the Kalu Ram vs State Of Rajasthan on 15 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94642787/
1 aforesaid reports, deserves to be suspended. 2.1. Learned counsel further submitted that all the evidence, including medical evidence produced before the learned Court below were not sufficient to prove the alleged offences against the applicant-appellant, because at the time of the alleged incident, the applicant-appellant was not present at the place of the incident in question, and therefore, the sentence awarded to the applicant/appellant deserves to be suspended.

On the other hand, learned Public Prosecutor, while opposing the suspension of sentence application, submitted that the applicant-appellant was convicted by the learned Trial Court, after taking into due consideration the overall facts and circumstances of the case and the evidence placed on record before it.
sentences._hearing_file: Kalu Ram vs State Of Rajasthan on 15 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: Thus, as per learned Public Prosecutor, the present second application for suspension of sentence ought not to be entertained by this Court.
sentences._hearing_file: Kalu Ram vs State Of Rajasthan on 15 January, 2024.json
Kalu Ram vs State Of Rajasthan on 15 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: It was further submitted that as per the medical report, it is clear that the abrasion and contusion were found on the private parts of the victim and the same was also recorded in the impugned judgment passed by the learned Court below.
sentences._hearing_file: Kalu Ram vs State Of Rajasthan on 15 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: Therefore, the applicant-appellant is not for indulgence of suspension of sentence awarded to him by the learned Court below.
sentences._hearing_file: Kalu Ram vs State Of Rajasthan on 15 January, 2024.json

sentences.text:
4. Heard learned counsel for the parties as well as perused the record of the case.
5.
sentences._hearing_file: Kalu Ram vs State Of Rajasthan on 15 January, 2024.json

sentences.text:
This Court finds that the first application for suspension of sentence of the present applicant-appellant was dismissed as not pressed by this Court vide order dated 23.09.2022 passed in S.B. Criminal Misc. Suspension of Sentence Application (Appeal) No.700/2022.
6.

entities.text: S.B. Criminal Misc. Suspension of Sentence Application (Appeal) No.700/2022
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences._hearing_file: Kalu Ram vs State Of Rajasthan on 15 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: This Court further finds that as per the record of the case including the medical report and FSL report, no evidence or proof has been produced on behalf of the applicant-appellant, which could even prima facie cast any shadow of doubt upon the impugned judgment passed by the learned Court below, and therefore, it is not a case where the indulgence of suspension of sentence deserves to be granted to the present applicant- appellant at this stage.
sentences._hearing_file: Kalu Ram vs State Of Rajasthan on 15 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: 7. This Court also finds that the applicant-appellant was convicted for commission of a heinous offence, and not in connection with any ordinary offence.
sentences._hearing_file: Kalu Ram vs State Of Rajasthan on 15 January, 2024.json

Thus, on a consideration of the overall facts and circumstances of the case as also the evidence available on [2024:RJ-JD:1084] (4 of 4) [SOSA-59/2023] record, this Court is not inclined to suspend the sentence awarded to the applicant-appellant vide the impugned judgment passed by the learned Court below.
sentences._hearing_file: Kalu Ram vs State Of Rajasthan on 15 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: 9. Consequently, the present second application for suspension of sentence is dismissed.

opennyai_summary.19_August_2023__facts: This application for bail has been filed by the petitioner under Section 439 of the Cr.P.C. in connection with FIR No.62/2023 Police Station Kaparda, District Jodhpur, for the offences under Sections 323, 354, 506, 376/G of IPC.
opennyai_summary.19_August_2023__arguments:
Learned counsel submitted that (2 of 2) [CRLMB-9848/2023] challan against the present petitioner has already been filed; the petitioner is in judicial custody since long and the trial of the case will take sufficiently long time, therefore, the benefit of bail may be granted to the accused-petitioner.
Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor and learned counsel for the complainant have opposed the bail application.
opennyai_summary.19_August_2023__ANALYSIS: However, they were not in position to refute the fact that aforementioned co- accused has already been enlarged on bail.
opennyai_summary.19_August_2023__decision:
Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and keeping in view the fact that co-accused- Sohan Lal @ Sethi has already been enlarged on bail by this Court and looking to the possibility that the trial may take long time to conclude, without expressing any opinion on merits/demerits of the case, this Court is inclined to enlarge the petitioner on bail.
Consequently, the bail application filed under Section 439 Cr.P.C. is allowed.
It is ordered that petitioner-Kalu Ram S/o Shri Jagdish Ram, arrested in connection with FIR No.62/2023 Police Station Kaparda, District Jodhpur; provided he executes a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/-
and two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the learned trial Court.
Petitioner shall be required to appear before that Court on all dates of hearing and as and when called upon to do so.
